notes.82v.22: 82v.23: 'caelorum', 'of the heavens', may be an error for 'colorum', 'of colours'. 'daz vreislich' (83r.2), 'the dangerous [one]', is unclear: a malignant sore, perhaps a carbuncle. 'sælige suht' (83r.3), 'blessed sickness', is probably epilepsy (the 'holy disease'). 'verstrætet' (83r.14) read as 'staunches'. 'allezane' (83r.18) read as 'always'.

nodes.text: violet; it gives off golden flames. These precious
stones signify men of flesh. The variety of the heavens is
the multiplicity of the virtues. Jasper is very effective
against a flow of blood, if it is put in wine and one drinks this; it helps.
If a woman drinks that into which this same stone has been thrown,
if she is not a maiden, she wets her feet; if
she is a maiden, it does her no harm. If the blister which you
think may be the dangerous kind, with this same stone
you scratch, it goes away. It is also good against the blessed sickness,
if one drinks the wine in which the stone lies.
It is also good for one who has the strong fever, if he
drinks of it. It is good for women who are to be delivered
of a child, if she then drinks [of it], or if over the navel
[it is] bound. It is good for one whose eyes suddenly hurt,
if he blesses himself with it three mornings, in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.
It is good for every kind of snakebite, if you lay it on
where the bite is: the venom comes out of the wound. It is
also good for one who has been poisoned, if he drinks chervil juice
in which this same stone lies: he vomits the poison at once. It is
also good in that it staunches the blood that from a wound
or the nose flows, if it is bound on there.
Any woman who has the stone on her finger so that it
touches the skin through [it] does not become pregnant. It is also good
for the leper, if he always carries it with him.
